card: Passes base32 I2P addresses directly to the SAM bridge STREAM CONNECT command, removing a redundant preliminary NAMING LOOKUP round trip on outbound I2P connections. When peer lookups fail under the old approach, empty responses are treated as local proxy errors rather than unreachable peers, preventing AddrMan from recording the failed connection attempt. SAM v3 supports base32 destinations directly across all supported I2P router versions. A unit test verifies connection behavior and error propagation.
changed_since_previous: Added a unit test covering direct base32 STREAM CONNECT and verifying that CANT_REACH_PEER and TIMEOUT responses are not treated as proxy errors.
evidence: PR description references the SAM v3 API specification confirming STREAM CONNECT supports .b32.i2p destinations directly.

PR description notes minimum router versions supporting direct base32 connect (Java I2P 0.9.48, i2pd 2.38.0) are older than the versions required for leaseset encryption types already adopted in #35696.
problem: Outbound I2P connections perform an unnecessary NAMING LOOKUP round trip to the SAM bridge before connecting. Furthermore, unresolvable peers result in an empty lookup reply which Bitcoin Core interprets as an internal proxy error, preventing AddrMan from recording the failed connection attempt.

risk.why: A bug or compatibility issue with the SAM bridge command could break outbound I2P connections for I2P users.

summary: Passes base32 I2P addresses directly into the SAM bridge STREAM CONNECT command, eliminating the intermediate NAMING LOOKUP query. This removes an extra round trip on every outbound I2P connection and ensures failed connections are classified as unreachable peers rather than proxy errors.
